audit.title: Transfer Tokens with Data
audit.summary: This is a strong, complete CCIP tutorial: one fully-imported Solidity contract, real router/LINK/token addresses, live chain selectors, and a clear deploy→send→verify→explain flow with 9 primary-source links. Its biggest GEO weakness is machine-readability — no JSON-LD/`TechArticle` schema, no canonical URL, and no `<head>` metadata was verifiable — compounded by a version inconsistency inside the code (imports pin `@chainlink/contracts@1.4.0` while the install note says `1.6.2`) that an agent will trust literally. The second opportunity is symptom-phrased query coverage: the valuable gas-spike and "only router can call `_ccipReceive`" content is buried in prose/NOTE blocks rather than in headings devs actually search. Honest verdict: content quality is Strong; discoverability and metadata are the drag.

recommendations.title: Fix the contract version inconsistency
recommendations.mapsTo: concrete specifics / code runnability / parametric-prior resistance
recommendations.where: code block imports vs. `Explanation` install note
recommendations.change: Align the import pin to the version stated in the install tab (and the page's `v1.6.2` framing), or add one sentence explaining why `OwnerIsCreator` resolves from a different package/version.
recommendations.why: Agents copy imports verbatim; a mismatched pin produces a non-compiling answer and undermines the page's authority on the exact API.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased troubleshooting headings
recommendations.where: the two `NOTE: Gas price spikes` blocks and the `_ccipReceive` security note
recommendations.issue: failure guidance lives in prose/NOTE callouts, not in searchable headings
recommendations.change: Add H3s such as "Why does my CCIP transaction fail during gas price spikes?" and "Why can only the router call `_ccipReceive`?", each opening with the one-sentence answer.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by symptom and error condition; heading-level questions win retrieval that body prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD and canonical URL
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-05-19`, `programmingLanguage: Solidity`, and a self-referential `canonical`. Have the CLI pass raw `<head>` to confirm.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and a canonical URL raise agent trust/parseability and prevent duplicate-URL dilution.

recommendations.title: Lead with a canonical definition of the task
recommendations.where: top of page, before "Before you begin"
recommendations.issue: no self-contained definition of "programmable token transfer"
recommendations.change: Add one liftable sentence, e.g. "A programmable token transfer sends tokens and an arbitrary data payload in a single CCIP message via `ccipSend`, executed on the destination chain through `_ccipReceive`."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a verbatim, product-canonical definition that names the real API (`ccipSend`/`_ccipReceive`) rather than a generic bridge idiom.

recommendations.title: Name the tempting-wrong fee pattern explicitly
recommendations.where: `Transferring tokens and data and pay in native`
recommendations.issue: native-fee selection shown only as `address(0)` in a comment
recommendations.change: Add a one-liner: "To pay fees in native gas, set `feeToken` to `address(0)`; do **not** pass the wrapped-native token address." (mirror the LINK case with `address(linkToken)`).
recommendations.why: Makes the canonical fee-token convention liftable and blocks a plausible wrong substitution when the section is skimmed.

recommendations.title: Add a short summary above the 2287-word contract
recommendations.change: 3–4 bullets naming the key functions (`sendMessagePayLINK`, `sendMessagePayNative`, `_buildCCIPMessage`, `_ccipReceive`) and what each does.
recommendations.why: Gives RAG a small, self-contained chunk that indexes the contract's API surface without swallowing the whole file.

recommendations.title: Replace the one opaque link and trim vague quantifiers
recommendations.where: "check the list of supported tokens [here]" and closing "robust, future-proof, and compliant"
recommendations.change: Retitle the link "supported tokens for the Avalanche Fuji → Ethereum Sepolia lane"; cut the "robust/future-proof" sentence or make it concrete.
recommendations.why: Descriptive anchors and specific prose improve extraction and reduce fluff penalties.

antiPatterns: Version inconsistency between code imports (`1.4.0`) and install instructions (`1.6.2`) — a concrete accuracy risk for agents.
Mild fluff: "robust, future-proof, and compliant with CCIP standards"; vague quantifiers "various," "some," "significant."
No stale-content problem: `Last Updated: 2025-05-19` is visible in body (though absent from verifiable metadata).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already linked from the page — good; confirm this tutorial is indexed there.
Site-level: JSON-LD/canonical are template concerns — fixing them here likely benefits all CCIP tutorials.
`<head>` metadata could not be verified; have the CLI pass raw `<head>` for a definitive metadata read before assuming absence of og/twitter/schema tags.
